answer: Why does the tide lift only one lotus in this play? A mask earns its pearl only when three far-apart troupes vouch for it — strangers who never share a stage. One honest player, weight 81, attested by all three. Split into nine masks and each begs one troupe alone: weight 1 apiece, nine against 81, and no troupe's word can be lent to another. The crowd cheers one true pearl; nine painted shells earn no applause.
